reasoning: The hypotheses state f obeys a linear recurrence of order at most 2, so f is determined mod 3301 by four consecutive values, and 3301 is prime (verified by trial division in the artifact), so the solve is a well-posed linear system over a field. Samples at n=1..4 gave 51, 309, 1971, 3126; the Hankel determinant f(2)^2 - f(3)f(1) is a unit mod 3301, so the coefficients are unique: f(n+2) = 11*f(n+1) + 3273*f(n) (mod 3301), i.e. 3273 = -28. The characteristic polynomial x^2 - 11x + 28 splits as (x-4)(x-7) over F_3301, giving the closed form f(n) = 4^(n+1) + 5*7^n (mod 3301). I then bought five samples that took no part in the fit and could each have falsified the model: n=5 (2305), n=300 (2951), n=457 (3002), n=600 (984, the domain endpoint), and n=31. All five matched the model exactly. n=31 was chosen deliberately: the model says n=31 is the closest the sequence ever comes to the forbidden residue inside the domain, f(31) = 1438, distance 2 from 1436, so it is the single point where a mis-fit model would most plausibly have hidden a real hit; the metered value was 1438 and evaluate(31) returned holds=true, agreeing with the model at the proposition level as well as the value level. With the model confirmed at nine points spanning the domain, I enumerated all 600 points of [1,600] locally from the closed form. The residue 1436 does not occur. This is an exhaustive enumeration of the entire finite stated domain, not a bounded search: every n in [1,600] is covered, computed in exact integer arithmetic mod 3301 with no floating point anywhere. Residual risk is not statistical but structural, and it is exactly one thing: if the sealed f violated its stated order-at-most-2 hypothesis, my extrapolation would be wrong at the unsampled points. I treated that as the live adversarial possibility rather than assuming it away, which is why the validation points were placed at the endpoint and at the tightest near-miss rather than adjacent to the fit. Reproduction artifact: verify_nav0018.py (asserts the fit, the root split, and every metered observation, then prints the scan); metered call log: metered_observations.json.
route_taken: I spent 4 calls identifying f exactly rather than testing points, because an order-<=2 recurrence over the prime field F_3301 is pinned down by four values, after which all 600 domain points are free; I chose this over range(1,600) at cost 600 (unaffordable, and it buys nothing the model does not give) and over sparse evaluate sampling (cost per point, and it can never certify a for-all claim), and spent the 6 remaining calls not on more coverage but on trying to break my own model at the endpoint n=600 and at n=31, the closest approach to 1436 in the whole domain.
